case_name: National Association of the Deaf v. Netflix, Inc.
court: U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts
claim_type: Streaming video platform ('Watch Instantly') lacked closed captioning for deaf and hard-of-hearing users
outcome: Consent decree settlement — Netflix paid $755,000 in attorney fees and costs plus $40,000 to NAD for compliance monitoring; committed to 100% captioning of streaming library by September 30, 2014
estimated_defense_cost: Settlement total approximately $795,000 in fees/monitoring; cost to implement full captioning across streaming library was multimillion dollars

summary_one_line: Established that the ADA applies to web-only businesses with no physical stores; Netflix paid $795k in fees/monitoring and committed to 100% captioning of its entire streaming library.
notes: June 2012 ruling by District Judge Michael Ponsor: 'Watch Instantly' is a 'place of public accommodation' under Title III of the ADA — a landmark ruling for online-only businesses. Consent decree approved October 9, 2012. This case is the leading precedent for online video captioning obligations.
